business_problem: Accenture wanted to scale AI across its own operations and client work, but needed a practical way to govern risks such as bias, hallucinations, privacy breaches, cyberattacks and unclear accountability so the company could build trust while still moving quickly on AI adoption.
solution_summary: Accenture operationalized responsible AI as a company-wide compliance program rather than a principles-only policy. The design starts with a formal governance structure and a published set of responsible AI principles that are applied to internal systems and client-facing work. Those principles are translated into workflow controls across four elements: AI governance and policy, AI risk assessment, systemic enablement for responsible AI testing, and ongoing monitoring and compliance. In practice that means multidisciplinary oversight, screening and assessment processes, controls embedded in purchasing and enterprise systems, and testing tools plus persona-based training for employees who work directly with AI. Accenture also added mandatory ethics and compliance training along with broader Technology Quotient learning so responsible AI becomes part of how the enterprise develops, deploys and monitors AI instead of an afterthought attached to individual projects.

solution_components.name: responsible AI compliance program
solution_components.role: Defines the enterprise process for activating, monitoring and enforcing responsible AI practices.

solution_components.name: AI governance structure
solution_components.role: Assigns leadership, policies, standards and multidisciplinary oversight for AI use.

solution_components.name: AI risk assessments
solution_components.role: Screen AI use cases and projects for ethical, regulatory and operational risks before deployment.

solution_components.name: testing tools
solution_components.role: Support systematic responsible-AI checks and compliance validation during development and operation.

data_flow: AI projects are screened through governance and risk-assessment processes before use, then pass through embedded controls and testing tools. Ongoing monitoring and compliance checks feed back into the responsible AI compliance program so policies, training and oversight can be updated as AI use scales.
business_outcome: Accenture created a repeatable governance framework for scaling AI more safely across its business and client engagements, helping it activate AI value while reducing compliance, privacy, security and bias risks that could undermine trust.
architecture_clues: The program is organized around four operating elements rather than a single policy statement.
Controls were embedded into purchasing and other enterprise processes.
Testing tools and persona-based training support responsible-AI validation.
Ongoing monitoring and quality assurance are part of the operational model after deployment.
